newsitem.title: GERMANY: Viag unit ups Computer 2000 stake. [Corrected 14:12 gmt]
newsitem.headline: Viag unit ups Computer 2000 stake. [Corrected 14:12 gmt]

text.p: German conglomerate Viag AG, through its Kloeckner & Co unit, has raised its controlling stake in personal computer wholesaler Computer 2000 AG to over 75 percent, the companies said on Friday.

Kloeckner took control of Computer 2000 in 1994 when it bought shares from Arend Oetker and the Colonia insurance group and increased its holding to 75.03 percent by buying shares from sellers which it declined to identify. (Viag corrects share sellers).
Raising the stake above three-quarters required Computer 2000 to make an announcement under German stock exchange rules, but a price was not named for the transaction.

Kloeckner said it increased its holding because it views the medium-term earnings outlook at Computer 2000 positively. The higher stake would help boost Computer 2000's position as Europe's leading computer wholesaler despite current problems.
Computer 2000, which is based in Munich, said back in August it was striking its dividend for the 1995-96 business year to September 30.
Results were hit by restructuring at U.S. unit AmeriQuest, as well as startup costs for new operations in Latin America.
The company said, however, that it still expected its pre-tax result to be positive and turnover would grow to 6.5 billion marks from 4.9 billion marks a year earlier.
Computer 2000 stock was down 2.50 marks in late trading on the Frankfurt stock exchange at 242.50 marks.
Viag shares -- hit already by the departure this week of utility RWE AG from its telecommunications partnership with British Telecom Plc -- were down 1.20 marks at 573.
